pins.name: RUN
pins.description: RP2040 enable, pulled up inside (~50 kΩ): short to ground to reset

pins.name: AGND
pins.description: analog ground for GP26-28 (join to GND when the ADC is not critical)

pins.name: ADC_VREF
pins.description: the ADC's reference, filtered 3.3 V on the board

pins.name: 3V3
pins.description: 3V3(OUT): the board's 3.3 V regulator output, keep loads under 300 mA

pins.name: 3V3_EN
pins.description: the regulator's enable, pulled up to VSYS (100 kΩ): short to ground to switch 3.3 V off

pins.name: VSYS
pins.description: the system supply, 1.8-5.5 V: from VBUS through a Schottky diode, or feed it here (through a diode when USB is used too)

pins.name: VBUS
pins.description: USB 5 V when the USB cable is plugged in (0 V otherwise)

parameters.conditions: whole board current from VBUS (5 V) running the hello_serial example (continuously transmitting characters), USB connected, GPIOs unconnected except GPIO0/1 to a debug probe; typical, not guaranteed; includes the on-board regulator's losses; the datasheet gives no clock or temperature for it

source.location: document p. 13, section 4.1.2 Typical Use Cases, Table 2, Hello_serial row

notes: Same header pinout and footprint as the Pico (RASPBERRY_PI_PICO); GPIOs are 3.3 V (RP2350's IOs tolerate 5 V only while powered, as inputs: do not rely on it). In PCBKit 3V3 is `P3V3`, 3V3_EN `P3V3_EN`.
The UART, I2C and SPI functions listed are those RP2040 and RP2350 share on each pin; RP2350 adds UART on more pins (its function F11), PIO2 and HSTX on GP12-GP19.
RP2350 A2 (early Pico 2 boards) erratum E9: an input with the internal pull-down can latch near 2.2 V; use an external pull-down of 8.2 kΩ or less where a pulled-down input matters.
Power: USB (VBUS → diode → VSYS), or 1.8-5.5 V into VSYS (through its own Schottky diode when USB is used too). 3V3 can feed sensors (under 300 mA).
Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W (SC1633) has this header pinout too, with GP23-GP25 and GP29 taken by its radio like the Pico W.
